title: Molecular Origins of pH Gradients in Charge-Regulated Biomolecular Condensates.
authors: Weng, Shuo-Lin; Rekhi, Shiv; Kim, Young C; Palmer, Jeremy C; Mittal, Jeetain
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
one_liner_zh: 该文提出b-CR-MC框架，用蒙特卡洛模拟结合电荷调控，研究FUS和PGL-3等无序蛋白凝聚体中的pH梯度和离子分布，揭示序列依赖的电化学微环境机制，属于无序蛋白凝聚体互作环境的物理模拟建模，与本课题高度相关。
abstract: Biomolecular condensates exhibit spontaneous electrochemical microenvironments characterized by asymmetric ion distributions and pH gradients that emerge from protein-sequence-dependent charge regulation. Despite their biological importance, mechanistic understanding of these microenvironments has been constrained by the absence of computationally tractable frameworks capable of treating proton exchange, counterion partitioning, and buffer equilibria on consistent thermodynamic footing. Here, we introduce the buffered Charge-Regulation Monte Carlo (b-CR-MC) framework, which couples grand-canonical exchange of ions and buffer species with explicit charge regulation of titratable residues. By extending the CR-MC ion-merging strategy to multicomponent reservoirs and employing the Restricted Primitive Model, b-CR-MC achieves computational efficiency while maintaining thermodynamic rigor, with quantitative agreement to the more expensive generalized G-RxMC approach. Applied to full-length FUS (net positive) and PGL-3 (net negative) under physiological conditions, the framework reveals sequence-dependent pH gradients: the dense phase of FUS exhibits an alkaline shift, while PGL-3 exhibits an acidic shift, in both cases driving the condensate interior toward the protein's isoelectric point. Slab-geometry simulations further resolve the Donnan potential and continuous ion profiles across the condensate interface, confirming the direction and magnitude of these electrochemical shifts. Additionally, we identify spatially resolved buffer depletion within dense phases, establishing that dynamic charge regulation is a primary determinant rather than a secondary correction to condensate electrochemistry. By establishing a sequence-resolved, thermodynamically consistent computational platform, b-CR-MC enables quantitative prediction of how mutations and post-translational modifications reprogram condensate microenvironments across biological and pathophysiological contexts.
abstract_zh: 生物分子凝聚体展现出自发的电化学微环境，其特征为不对称离子分布和pH梯度，这些源于蛋白质序列依赖的电荷调控。尽管其具有生物学重要性，但由于缺乏能够在一致热力学基础上处理质子交换、反离子分配和缓冲液平衡的计算可处理框架，对这些微环境的机制理解一直受到限制。在此，我们引入了缓冲电荷调控蒙特卡洛（b-CR-MC）框架，该框架将离子和缓冲物种的大正则交换与可滴定残基的显式电荷调控相结合。通过将CR-MC离子合并策略扩展到多组分储库，并采用受限原始模型，b-CR-MC在保持热力学严谨性的同时实现了计算效率，与更昂贵的广义G-RxMC方法定量一致。在生理条件下应用于全长FUS（净正电荷）和PGL-3（净负电荷）时，该框架揭示了序列依赖的pH梯度：FUS的致密相表现出碱性偏移，而PGL-3表现出酸性偏移，在两种情况下均驱动凝聚体内部趋向蛋白质的等电点。平板几何模拟进一步解析了跨凝聚体界面的Donnan电位和连续离子分布，确认了这些电化学偏移的方向和幅度。此外，我们识别了致密相内空间分辨的缓冲液耗竭，确立了动态电荷调控是凝聚体电化学的主要决定因素，而非次要修正。通过建立序列分辨、热力学一致的计算平台，b-CR-MC能够定量预测突变和翻译后修饰如何在生物学和病理生理学背景下重编程凝聚体微环境。
